title: BLT
subtitle: Bacon, lettuce, and tomato sandwich on toasted white bread
excerpt: A BLT is crisp streaky bacon, a leaf of cos lettuce, and sliced ripe tomato on toasted white bread with mayonnaise. The balance depends on two things: the bacon must be cooked until properly crisp, and the tomato must be in season.
sourceNotes: American diner tradition. The BLT appears in American cookery writing from the early twentieth century, becoming a diner menu staple by the 1950s. General technique from Fannie Farmer, The Boston Cooking-School Cook Book (1896), Project Gutenberg.

content.text: A BLT is three ingredients on toast: crisp streaky bacon, ripe tomato, and a leaf of cos lettuce, with enough mayonnaise to hold everything together. It works because each element plays a distinct role: crunch from the bacon, acidity and moisture from the tomato, cool freshness from the lettuce. The bread must be toasted.

items.prepNote: outer leaves only, washed and dried

content.text: Lay the {{streaky-bacon}} of streaky bacon strips flat in a cold dry pan. Turn the heat to medium. Cook for 4 to 5 minutes per side until the fat has rendered and the edges are crisp. Drain on kitchen paper.
Toast the bread slices until golden. Spread each slice generously with {{mayonnaise}} of mayonnaise.
Season the sliced tomatoes with salt and pepper. Layer lettuce on 2 of the bread slices, then the tomatoes, then the bacon, then close with the other bread slices. Cut in half and serve at once.

items.cause: Pan started hot and the bacon crisped unevenly, or it was not cooked long enough.
items.fix: Start in a cold pan over medium heat. The fat renders gradually and the bacon crisps as the fat cooks off. Give it the full time on each side.

items.cause: Tomatoes placed directly against the bread with no barrier, releasing liquid.
items.fix: Put the lettuce leaf on the bread first to act as a moisture barrier between the tomato and the toast.

items.cause: Sliced too thick or rounds rather than crossways.
items.fix: Slice the tomato across the equator about 5 mm thick. Pat with kitchen paper to remove excess moisture.

content.text: An avocado BLT adds half a sliced avocado. A turkey BLT replaces bacon with sliced roast turkey and works well out of summer tomato season. Hot sauce in the mayonnaise adds heat. Back bacon gives a leaner result. Ciabatta or sourdough hold up better to extra fillings.

The BLT is one of the most ordered sandwiches in American diners and short-order counters, and one of the few dishes where the quality of the ingredients is the whole recipe. A winter tomato makes a mediocre BLT. A summer one, sliced thick and salted, makes a very good one. The bacon needs to be crisp, not chewy: the texture contrast is what separates a good BLT from a disappointing one.
